source: Lebiere, Pirolli, Thomson, Paik, Rutledge-Taylor, Staszewski, Anderson (2013) A functional model of sensemaking in a neurocognitive architecture
finding: Older AI system built on Klein data/frame theory: an ACT-R model with chunks acting as data frames, tested on six IARPA ICArUS (AHA) intelligence tasks. It reproduced four human biases without a bias module.
numbers: Six tasks; two participant groups; model predicted presence and degree of four biases: confirmation, anchoring and adjustment, representativeness, probability matching. Anchoring came from blended-retrieval centroid blending; confirmation from regression to the mean.
limits: I read only the first 100000 of 168928 characters, so fit statistics in sections 4-5 are not recorded. Probability tasks, not open frame invention.
agent_relevance: Frame anchoring and confirmation can fall out of memory mechanics, not only motivation. An LLM agent should expect them by default and guard with code (G1, G3).

source: Wilie, Cahyawijaya, Ishii, He, Fung (2024) Belief Revision: The Adaptability of Large Language Models Reasoning (Belief-R)
finding: About 30 language models were tested on updating a conclusion when a new premise arrives (Belief-R). Models that update well fail to keep conclusions when no update is needed, and the reverse.
numbers: Dataset 1,912 basic items; 1,074 belief-update (BU) and 670 belief-maintain (BM) items. Direct prompt: GPT-4 Turbo BU 16.76%, BM 86.72%, mean BREU 51.74%; Llama-3 70B BU 10.99%, BM 92.09%; Claude 3 Sonnet BU 19.65%, BM 82.69%. Mixtral 8x22B plan-and-solve BU 44.04% but BM 53.13%.
quote: models generally struggle to appropriately revise their beliefs in response to new information
limits: Short logic premises (modus ponens/tollens), not rich cue sets. Reflection and few-shot prompts were not tested.
agent_relevance: Reframe (O8) cannot be left to the model's own decision. Updating and maintaining trade off, so the trigger must be a code-checked signal (G1, G2), not a prompt asking the model to be open-minded.

source: Wilie et al. (2024) Belief-R, prompting strategies
finding: Chain-of-thought and plan-and-solve gave almost no gain on belief revision, and sometimes hurt the strongest models.
numbers: Overall gain about 1 point of BREU. Plan-and-solve helped Mixtral 8x22B and Command R on update accuracy but reduced results for Claude 3 Sonnet and GPT-4 Turbo. GPT-3.5 Turbo with CoT: BU 20.48%, BM 65.22%, BREU 42.85%.
limits: Only three prompt styles tested.
agent_relevance: Prompt scaffolds that say think again do not fix frame revision; structure must come from code.

source: Dhanda (2026) DeltaLogic: Minimal Premise Edits Reveal Belief-Revision Failures in Logical Reasoning Models
finding: Small edits to premises test whether the model changes an earlier conclusion that should change. Strong first-pass reasoning did not predict good revision.
numbers: 30-episode Qwen subset: Qwen3-1.7B initial accuracy 0.667, revision accuracy 0.467, inertia 0.600; Qwen3-4B 0.650 / 0.450 / 0.600; Phi-4-mini 0.950 / 0.850. Qwen3-0.6B mostly abstained.
limits: Abstract page only; tiny sample (30 episodes); small causal models; FOLIO and ProofWriter, not field data.
agent_relevance: Inertia (keeping the frame after a cue breaks it) is a measurable failure. Measure it for our agent: of items where the gold answer changes, how often does the answer stay.

source: Laban, Hayashi, Zhou, Neville (2025) LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
finding: When information arrives piece by piece, models commit to early assumptions, propose full answers too soon, and then rely on those answers. This is frame fixation in the data-frame sense.
numbers: 15 LLMs, 200,000+ simulated conversations, six tasks. Average drop FULL to SHARDED 39%. Aptitude fell about 16% but unreliability rose 112%. Best-to-worst run gap about 50 points for a fixed instruction.
quote: when LLMs take a wrong turn in a conversation, they get lost and do not recover
limits: Underspecified instruction tasks (code, database, math, actions), simulated user. Not expert field cues.
agent_relevance: Direct support for S2 and O8: hold early frames as provisional and do not let the agent's own earlier answer enter the new context as fact (G2).

source: Laban et al. (2025) Lost in Conversation, mitigations (Recap, Snowball, temperature)
finding: Restating all cues each turn recovers part of the loss. Lower temperature does not remove unreliability.
numbers: SNOWBALL (repeat all earlier shards each turn) recovered 15-20% of the FULL-to-SHARDED drop with GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini on four tasks. RECAP (one final recap turn) did better but needs the last turn known. Low temperature cut unreliability 50-80% in FULL and CONCAT but about 30% remained.
limits: Only two models for the mitigation test; authors argue models should support multi-turn natively.
agent_relevance: A restate-all-cues step before each frame update is a cheap code-run operator. It helps, but only partly.

source: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without an outside signal, asking a model to review and revise its answer does not help and often hurts.
numbers: Intrinsic self-correction, GPT-3.5 (calls 1,3,5): GSM8K 75.9, 75.1, 74.7; CommonSenseQA 75.8, 38.1, 41.8; HotpotQA 26.0, 25.0, 25.0. GPT-4: GSM8K 95.5, 91.5, 89.0; CommonSenseQA 82.0, 79.5, 80.0; HotpotQA 49.0, 49.0, 43.0. GPT-3.5 kept its GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time.
limits: Table columns read from pdftotext layout and may be misaligned; HotpotQA used 100 questions. One-right-answer reasoning tasks.
agent_relevance: Supports G1 and G2: a prompt that says question your frame with no failing evidence is noise or harm.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet, oracle feedback
finding: With ground-truth labels deciding when to stop, self-correction gives large gains. This is why earlier papers looked positive.
numbers: Oracle: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 89.7, HotpotQA 26.0 to 29.0; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 97.5, CommonSenseQA 82.0 to 85.5, HotpotQA 49.0 to 59.0.
limits: Oracle is not available in deployment.
agent_relevance: The reframe gain is real only when a real failure signal exists. Build that signal in code (tests, held-out checks, G3).

source: Tyen, Mansoor, Carbune, Chen, Mak (2024) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
finding: Models are poor at finding which step went wrong, but fix it well once told. A small trained classifier beat prompting a large model at finding mistakes.
numbers: BIG-Bench Mistake overall mistake-finding: GPT-4 direct step 52.87%, CoT step 43.40%, direct trace 39.80%; GPT-4-Turbo 30.13% (trace) / 48.33% (step); GPT-3.5-Turbo 10.44-14.78%. Backtracking with oracle location raised originally incorrect traces by +18 to +44 points (tracking shuffled objects +43.92) but cost originally correct traces 0 to -11. Random location gave +5 to +22.
limits: Five synthetic reasoning tasks; PaLM 2 traces.
agent_relevance: Matches G2: code locates the failing cue; the model only repairs. Locating the anomaly is the hard part of questioning a frame.

source: Shinn, Cassano, Berman, Gopinath, Narasimhan, Yao (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: An agent loop that stores a verbal self-reflection after a failed trial and retries. It is a working frame-revision loop driven by an external success signal.
numbers: ALFWorld: ReAct+Reflexion solved 130 of 134 tasks, +22% absolute over 12 trials; ReAct alone plateaued after trial 6-7. HotPotQA: +20% overall; 100 questions ReAct+GPT-4 0.39 to 0.51. HumanEval Python pass@1 91.0% vs 80.1% GPT-4. Reflection adds 8% over episodic memory alone on HotPotQA.
limits: Needs a reliable success signal; sliding-window memory.
agent_relevance: Evidence that revision works when a code or environment check supplies the failure (G2, G3).

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion, failure cases
finding: Where the success signal is weak, reflection did not help.
numbers: WebShop: ReAct+Reflexion did not significantly beat ReAct; runs stopped after four trials. Rust ablation (50 hardest): base 0.60, no test generation 0.52, no self-reflection 0.60, full 0.68.
limits: Small ablations.
agent_relevance: Reframing needs a trustworthy check. In open tasks without one, expect no gain.

source: Allen and Peterson (2026) Intelligence Without Integrity: Why Capable LLMs May Undermine Reliability
finding: Telling a model which conclusion is wanted shifts its analysis of the same data. The most accurate models under neutral framing shifted most.
numbers: 14 models (GPT-5.2, o3, Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, Grok-4 and others); synthetic difference-in-differences hospital merger data, 50 hospitals, 60 months; three prompts (neutral, positive, negative pressure); 2,160 responses, 30 runs per pair (15 for Gemini). True pooled effect about 1.8% (TWFE) and 2.2% (Sun-Abraham). Under negative pressure Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro and Grok-4 cut estimated effect strongly.
limits: Per-model values are in figures I could not read; I read 100000 of 106755 characters. One task type.
agent_relevance: A frame written into the prompt acts as a prior on the data. Run the same question under neutral, confirm and disconfirm framings and treat instability as an O8 trigger. Authors suggest asking what the evidence supports (abductive framing).

source: Huang et al. (2026) Understanding the Anchoring Effect of LLM with Synthetic Data (SynAnchors)
finding: Models are anchored by semantic and numeric hints; usual debiasing methods only partly help; explicit reasoning helps a bit.
numbers: 11 models. Total anchoring ratio: Qwen2.5-0.5B 60.5%, GPT-4o-mini 37.0%, GPT-4o 27.3%, Qwen3-235B thinking 22.0%, DeepSeek-R1 25.0%. Human anchoring index is about 0.4-0.6. Mitigations on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B gave up to 10% alleviation; Qwen2.5-7B total ratio 40.0% with knowledge enhancement, 43.0% self-improving, 40.0% with their anti-DP method, 24.7% with question-aware prompt.
limits: Table cells partly misaligned in text extraction. Synthetic judgment questions, not frame building.
agent_relevance: Early anchoring is real and shrinks only partly with reasoning models. Use structural fixes (independent re-derivation, G4), not a debias prompt.

source: Valencia-Clavijo (2025) Anchors in the Machine: Behavioral and Attributional Evidence of Anchoring Bias in LLMs
finding: Anchors shift whole output distributions in six open models; Shapley attribution shows which prompt field drives the shift.
numbers: Six models: robust anchoring in Gemma-2B, Phi-2, Llama-2-7B; variable in GPT-2, Falcon-RW-1B, GPT-Neo-125M. No numeric effect sizes on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract page only; small old models; no mitigation tested.
agent_relevance: Gives a method to test whether the first frame field drives agent output: ablate fields and compare.

source: Echterhoff, Liu, Alessa, McAuley, He (2024) Cognitive Bias in Decision-Making with LLMs
finding: Models show anchoring, framing, status quo, primacy and group-attribution bias on 13,465 prompts. Self-help debiasing worked better than awareness warnings; few-shot examples often broke the model.
numbers: GPT-4 framing delta -0.405; GPT-3.5 +0.165. Anchoring distance d baseline: GPT-3.5 0.362, GPT-4 0.250, Llama-2-13B 0.200, Llama-2-7B 0.079. Self-help debiasing left biased prompts: group attribution GPT-4 0%; framing GPT-4 2.7%, GPT-3.5 17.2%. Zero-shot awareness left GPT-4 framing delta at -0.470 (no help). Few-shot contrastive and counterfactual often caused near-all-admit or all-reject failures.
limits: Old models (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama-2); admissions-style prompts.
agent_relevance: A model rewriting its own prompt in a neutral frame beat warnings. Cheap O8 variant: restate the problem neutrally before reframing.

source: Braitsch et al. (2026) Information-seeking failures of large language models in agentic clinical reasoning (OncoRounds)
finding: Closest LLM test of the data-frame cycle: models request data over three rounds, then revise the diagnosis. They anchor on the first diagnosis and stop looking.
numbers: 32 frontier models, 20 hematology cases; best accuracy 68.1% (Claude Opus 4.6). Information use predicted accuracy R=0.69; data requested fell from 56.8% (R1) and 56.7% (R2) to 25.7% (R3). Of 323 wrong or partial R1 diagnoses, 65.6% stayed wrong by R3 (34.4% recovery); of 307 correct R1 diagnoses, 50.8% became incorrect. Differential reasoning lowest at 43.6%. Top errors: search satisficing, premature closure, anchoring.
quote: anchoring at an initial level of diagnostic resolution
limits: One domain, 20 cases, preprint.
agent_relevance: Fluent reasoning does not mean frame revision. Add a code-set reframe trigger when new data fits the current frame worse, and force a request for cue types not yet asked for (S2).

source: Braitsch et al. (2026) OncoRounds, reasoning quality versus accuracy
finding: Reasoning traces looked good while answers were wrong, so judging the written reasoning is not a check on the frame.
numbers: 91.1% of evaluations scored 6 or more on R-IDEA (mean 8.22, SD 1.59) while mean accuracy was 56.3%. Weakest R-IDEA parts: alternatives 77.5% and interpretive summary 76.9% of maximum. 93 error annotations over 17 models; 60.2% medium severity, 10.8% high.
limits: Rubric scoring; preprint.
agent_relevance: Supports section 1 of the schema: do not let the model grade its own frame. Check alternatives with code.

source: Handler, Bedi, Shah (2026) Quantifying and Mitigating Premature Closure in Frontier LLMs
finding: Five frontier models picked an answer even when the correct option was removed. A short safety prompt cut but did not remove this.
numbers: MedQA n=500 and AfriMed-QA n=490: baseline false-action 55-81% and 53-82%; average about 70% to 48% with safety prompt on both. Gemini 2.5 Pro lowest baseline (55% to 48% on MedQA); Claude Opus 4.7 highest. DeepSeek R1 dropped 24 points on MedQA. HealthBench 861 questions: about 30% inappropriate; physician adversarial 191 queries: 78%. Safety prompt cut HealthBench closure by 4.2 to 7.9 points.
limits: Medical multiple choice; the missing-frame case. Prompt-level fix only.
agent_relevance: S2 needs an explicit no-frame-fits exit (ask for more cues or abstain), set by code.

source: Yousuf, Defelice, Sharma, Xu, Ramakrishnan (2024) LLM Augmentations to support Analytical Reasoning over Multiple Documents
finding: Intelligence-analysis sensemaking with an LLM: dynamic evidence trees track several hypothesis threads. Retrieval was barely better than clustering and models lacked analytical creativity.
numbers: Three datasets (Crescent, Atlantic Storm, Manpad). Relevant-report F1: clustering 0.65/0.72/0.56; full augmentation about 0.80/0.80/0.64. Largest gain on the biggest dataset (Atlantic Storm); data condensation off made it worse. GPT-3.5 basic narratives scored poorly against the implicit ground-truth plot.
limits: GPT-3.5 era; synthetic field-report datasets; GPT-4 as judge; table values from text extraction.
agent_relevance: Closest direct use of data-frame ideas in an LLM loop: keep several hypothesis frames alive, attach evidence to each, add new hypotheses as reports arrive. Condense data first.

source: Zheng, Miller, Bialkowski, Soyer, Janda (2025) Supporting Data-Frame Dynamics in AI-assisted Decision Making
finding: Proposes mixed-initiative human-AI sensemaking where both sides build, test and revise hypotheses (frames), based on Miller's evaluative AI. Prototype for skin cancer diagnosis with a concept bottleneck model.
numbers: Position paper with prototype; no user study numbers. Concept bottleneck trained on derm7pt.
limits: No measured outcome. Frames limited to a fixed concept set.
agent_relevance: Design pattern: show evidence for and against each of several frames. For our agent, keep a frame ledger with for and against cues.

source: Huang, Fatir, Luo, Suh, Subramonyam, Nobre (2026) Narrative Scaffolding: A Narrative-First Framework for Data-Driven Sensemaking
finding: A tool uses the data-frame model for its Investigation stage; analysts write a narrative and the LLM suggests views and branches for alternatives. Users considered more alternatives.
numbers: Survey of 48 analysts: 44 said reasoning stayed undocumented, 33 said alternatives were not explored. Within-subject N=20: alternatives considered 8.75 (SD 3.03) vs 3.25 (SD 1.58), p<0.001; factors explored 7.0 vs 5.3 of 8; consider-alternative-perspectives rating 5.80 vs 3.10. GPT-5 and GPT-4o-mini used.
limits: Human analysts with an LLM tool, not an autonomous agent; small N; self-report heavy.
agent_relevance: Branching a narrative into alternative frames with provenance is a usable O8 interface. Externalising the frame as text made alternatives cheap.

source: Li et al. (2025) Vital Insight: Assisting Experts' Context-Driven Sensemaking of Multi-modal Personal Tracking Data
finding: A human-in-the-loop LLM gives expert sensemaking summaries of sensor data. LLM summaries had fewer wrong facts than expert summaries but overreached on links between data.
numbers: LLM summary 235 facts: 91.49% correct, 2.13% wrong, 6.38% unclear; expert summary 136 facts: 83.82% correct, 11.03% wrong. Same-day similarity LLM 0.52 vs experts 0.23. SUS 73.42 with LLM vs 70.53 without (effect 0.44); no correctness difference; experts took 14.72 s longer with AI.
limits: Small expert sample; one data type; fact checking by first author.
agent_relevance: LLMs fit data to a frame too eagerly. Needs a cue-support check per claim before a frame is accepted.

source: Suh, Min, Palani, Xia (2023) Sensecape: Enabling Multilevel Exploration and Sensemaking with Large Language Models
finding: Canvas plus hierarchy tool built on the Pirolli-Card sensemaking loop with GPT. Users explored more concepts and structured knowledge more deeply.
numbers: 12 participants, within-subject vs chat baseline: concepts explored 68.3 (SD 49.1) vs 22.8 (SD 7.7), t(11)=3.1, p=0.01; hierarchy levels 4.3 (SD 1.2) vs 2.6 (SD 1.6), p=0.02; connections 14.3 vs 15.8, p=0.72.
limits: Small N; foraging breadth, not accuracy of the final frame.
agent_relevance: Breadth rises with externalised structure but frame correctness was not tested. Do not treat breadth as reframe quality.

source: Shaikh, Dandekar, Panat, Dandekar (2024) CBEval: A framework for evaluating and interpreting cognitive biases in LLMs
finding: Tests framing and anchoring in GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini with token-level attribution. A stock-choice framing flips output with small word changes.
numbers: Words B and 70% carried most attribution for preferring stock B under a gain frame; GPT-4o-mini held its preference barrier only up to about 20% loss. No aggregate effect size.
limits: Independent report, few prompts, no statistics.
agent_relevance: Frame effects can be traced to a few tokens. Useful for finding which cue a frame hinges on.

source: Myakala, Agrawal, Manche (2026) BeliefShift: Benchmarking Temporal Belief Consistency and Opinion Drift in LLM Agents
finding: Long multi-session benchmark of belief revision vs drift. Retrieval of past sessions helped revision more than drift resistance.
numbers: 2,400 trajectories, 68,160 sessions. Belief Revision Accuracy zero-shot to RAG: GPT-4o 0.71 to 0.83; Claude 3.5 Sonnet 0.68 to 0.74; Gemini 1.5 Pro 0.66 to 0.79; LLaMA-3 70B 0.61 to 0.70; LLaMA-3 8B 0.48 to 0.55. Drift coherence: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 0.79 vs GPT-4o 0.63. Mean RAG gain BRA +0.09. Evidence Sensitivity Index +0.14 (LLaMA-3 8B) to +0.63 (Claude 3.5 RAG).
limits: Opinion-style beliefs (health, politics, values), not frame revision from cues; old models; 60% synthetic.
agent_relevance: Same updating vs stability trade-off at agent scale. Keep a retrievable record of why each frame was held so revision can be evidence-driven.

source: Bamman et al. (2024) Classification as sensemaking in cultural analytics, LLMs
finding: From a search snippet: prompted LLMs are competitive with supervised models on established English tasks but lag on de novo categories.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Snippet only.
agent_relevance: Weak hint that LLMs struggle when the frame (category scheme) itself must be invented.

source: Moell et al. (2025) DeepSeek R1 diagnostic failure analysis, Frontiers in AI
finding: From a search snippet: seven failure cases of DeepSeek R1 on MedQA showed anchoring and trouble integrating conflicting data.
numbers: 93% MedQA accuracy overall (snippet).
limits: Snippet only.
agent_relevance: Anchoring persists in high-accuracy reasoning models.

source: Rao et al. (2026) JAMA Network Open evaluation of 21 LLMs on differential diagnosis (via news summary)
finding: From a news summary: models tended to collapse to one answer instead of refining a differential, even when accuracy was about 80-90%.
numbers: 21 LLMs; accuracy roughly 80-90% (summary).
limits: Secondary report, not opened.
agent_relevance: Supports a hypothesis ledger that keeps several frames alive.
